title: Grateful Dead Live at Manhattan Center on 1971-04-05
lineage: Panasonic SV-3700 > Cardas cable S/PDIF > Edirol UA-5 > USB > WaveLab @ [32bit float / 48kHz] Mastering: In WaveLab with iZotope Ozone 3 Rate Conversion with r8brain to [16bit/44.1kHz] > CD Wave > TLH > Flac
source: 7" two track reel @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) PCM501ES analog out > dolby A decoder > analog in PCMF1 > analog out > Fostex D5 Dat @ 48 kHz

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of an early‑71 set with a rare China Rider, monster Big Railroad Blues solo and the first live Sing Me Back Home.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers crystal‑clear soundboard quality that lets listeners hear every nuance of this early‑1971 performance. Highlights include a rare China Rider, a scorching Big Railroad Blues solo, the debut of "Sing Me Back Home" and a tight second set capped by The Other One and Bertha. Pigpen’s presence is celebrated throughout, and despite one note about vocal splicing, the show feels vibrant and historic.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high reviewer scores (mostly 5‑star) and enthusiastic comments about both performance and soundboard quality indicate an outstanding show with excellent recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with no reported dropouts; a minor comment about vocal splicing but overall clear and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Rare early‑show gem (China Rider) followed by a powerful second set; Bertha is squeezed in near the end, keeping momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar solo on Big Railroad Blues is praised as monster and later used on Skull & Roses.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for changing a battery during the first "Sing Me Back Home" while the band works out the arrangement.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ/vocals are repeatedly thanked, highlighting his contribution to the show’s vibe.
